original_question: Is a C0-semigroup with generator A immediately norm continuous if and only if ||R(is, A)|| tends to 0 as |s| tends to infinity?
target_in_paper: Section 2 (Regularity), Problem 9: "Characterization of immediate norm continuity by the resolvent." The adjoining comment states that this problem was answered negatively by Chill–Tomilov and independently by Mátrai.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core statement almost verbatim: it identifies the correct semigroup class (a C0-semigroup), the generator A, the exact resolvent condition along the imaginary axis, and the intended biconditional with immediate norm continuity. This is the right target in the paper.
missing_details: The paper-wide ambient setting is a one-parameter strongly continuous semigroup on a Banach space X; your draft does not explicitly name the Banach space or the semigroup notation (for example, (T(t))_{t\ge 0}).

To make the question stand-alone, 'immediately norm continuous' should be spelled out as: the map t \mapsto T(t) is continuous in operator norm for every t>0, i.e. on (0,\infty), not necessarily at t=0.
The resolvent notation should be defined explicitly: R(\lambda,A)=(\lambda I-A)^{-1}.
The variable s should be stated to range over real numbers, so the limit is taken along the imaginary axis \lambda=is with s\in\mathbb R.

Strictly speaking, the condition \|R(is,A)\|\to 0 presupposes that is lies in the resolvent set for all sufficiently large |s| (or that the limit is understood along the imaginary axis where the resolvent is defined).

If one wants full ambient precision, the field is implicit in the paper; because the question uses is and the resolvent on the imaginary axis, one normally works over a complex Banach space (or the complexification of a real one).
The paper records this as a historical 'prove or disprove' problem and immediately notes that the answer is negative, so it is not presented there as a currently open conjecture.
refined_question: Let (T(t))_{t\ge 0} be a C0-semigroup on a Banach space X with generator A. Is T immediately norm continuous—that is, is the map t\mapsto T(t) continuous from (0,\infty) into \mathcal L(X) in operator norm—if and only if \|R(is,A)\|\to 0 as |s|\to\infty for real s, where R(\lambda,A)=(\lambda I-A)^{-1}?
justification: The draft matches Section 2, Problem 9 of the paper, whose title is exactly about characterizing immediate norm continuity by resolvent decay. The paper-wide abstract fixes the ambient setting as C0-semigroups on Banach spaces, and the local comment under Problem 9 adds the important status update that the statement was later disproved. Since the nearby context does not broaden the problem beyond this biconditional, the refined version only makes the hidden notation and definitions explicit, without changing scope.
